def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input:
## Definition

A **finite gate alphabet** is a finite list of distinct labels, each assigned
one exact matrix in $SU(2):=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=I_2,\det M=1\}$. A
**Cauchy name** for a target $U\in SU(2)$ is a
deterministic procedure which, on unary input $1^b$, returns a rational
$2\times2$ complex matrix $Q_b$ whose real and imaginary entries differ from
the corresponding entries of $U$ by at most $2^{-b}$. The name has a stated
time bound $T(b)$. A precision request is a positive rational
$\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ in binary, using the effective encoding convention of
[[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

The Cauchy name specifies the exact target through all its approximants; an
individual $Q_b$ need not be unitary. An exact-real target handle and a
Cauchy-name input are distinct interfaces: the first permits ideal exact
comparisons, while a finite Turing implementation must use the second.
def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set:
## Definition

Write $SU(2):=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=I_2,\det M=1\}$. An
**inverse-closed dense $SU(2)$ gate package** consists of a finite set
$G\subset SU(2)$ of exact matrices with finite labels such that $g^{-1}=g^*$
belongs to $G$ for each $g\in G$ and the subgroup $\langle G\rangle$ of finite
products is dense in $SU(2)$ in operator norm. A word is a finite ordered list
of labels; its value is the corresponding matrix product, and its length is
the number of labels.

For a compiler package, also fix a rational $0<\eta_0<1/4096$, a finite list
$\mathcal N_0$ of words, and an integer $L_0$ such that every $U\in SU(2)$ is
within operator-norm distance $\eta_0/4$ of the value of some word in
$\mathcal N_0$, and every listed word has length at most $L_0$. This is a
finite **base-net certificate**. Density proves that such a certificate
exists, but does not compute the list or its maximum word length.
lem-qc-fixed-dimension-interval-arithmet:
## Statement

Fix a positive matrix dimension $d$ and an integer $c\ge1$. A dyadic interval is a
closed interval with dyadic-rational endpoints; a complex matrix interval
stores one such interval for every real and imaginary entry. Suppose each
input is given by a Cauchy procedure which, on unary request $1^q$, returns a
rational approximation to each real and imaginary entry with error at most
$2^{-q}$ and uses $O((q+1)^c)$ bit operations. Suppose exact scalar and
matrix inputs have entries of modulus at most $3$. Each fixed algebraic real
constant is supplied by a rational polynomial and an open rational interval
with nonroot endpoints on which the polynomial has opposite endpoint signs
and exactly one real root.
When each scalar divisor
and each norm used for normalization has modulus at
least $2^{-B}$, the following routines return dyadic intervals of diameter at
most $2^{-p}$ containing the exact answer, using
$O((p+B+1)^{\max(c,3)})$ bit operations:

- any fixed finite composition of sums and products;
- quotient by a scalar whose modulus is at least $2^{-B}$;
- the nonnegative square root of a real in $[0,1]$;
- normalization $v/\|v\|_2$ of a real vector with $\|v\|_2\ge2^{-B}$;
- the matrix exponential $e^A$ when $\|A\|\le1$; and
- the matrix logarithm $\log(I+E)=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^{j+1}E^j/j$
  when $\|E\|\le1/2$.

Here $d$ and the number of scalar operations in the fixed composition are
constants. The exponent $B$ is needed only for divisions and normalization;
the square-root routine also works at input zero. The constants in the
complexity bound may depend on the fixed dimension, routine, and Cauchy-time
constant.
lem-qc-irrational-rotation-dense-on-circ:
## Statement

If $\alpha\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$, then
$\{e^{2\pi i n\alpha}:n\in\mathbb Z\}$ is dense in the unit circle.
lem-qc-su2-near-identity-logarithm:
## Statement

For a matrix $M$, write $e^M=\sum_{j\ge0}M^j/j!$. Here
$SU(2):=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=I_2,\det M=1\}$. If
$D\in SU(2)$ and $\|D-I\|\le\rho\le1/2$, then the operator-norm
convergent series
$$\log D=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{j+1}(D-I)^j/j$$
satisfies $e^{\log D}=D$, is traceless and skew-Hermitian, and
$\|\log D\|\le-\log(1-\rho)\le2\rho$.
lem-qc-compact-su2-base-net:
## Statement

For every $\delta>0$ and every finite $G\subset SU(2)$ whose generated
subgroup is dense, there is a finite list of words in $G$ whose values form a
$\delta$-net of $SU(2)$. The maximum length of the words in that finite list
is finite. This is an existence statement; it does not compute a net from the
density hypothesis.
lem-qc-pauli-vector-multiplication:
## Statement

For the Pauli matrices $X,Y,Z$ in
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], the matrices
are Hermitian, traceless, and square to $I$. For $u,v\in\mathbb R^3$, writing
$u\cdot\sigma=u_1X+u_2Y+u_3Z$ gives
$$ (u\cdot\sigma)(v\cdot\sigma)=(u\cdot v)I+i(u\times v)\cdot\sigma.$$
Also, the Pauli triple is a real basis of the traceless Hermitian $2\times2$
matrices, $\|u\cdot\sigma\|=|u|$, and the commutator therefore satisfies
$$[iu\cdot\sigma,iv\cdot\sigma]=-2i(u\times v)\cdot\sigma.$$
lem-qc-su2-balanced-commutator:
## Statement

For a matrix $M$, write $e^M=\sum_{j\ge0}M^j/j!$. Here
$SU(2):=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=I_2,\det M=1\}$. If
$D\in SU(2)$ and $0\le\|D-I\|\le\eta\le1/16$, there are
$V,W\in SU(2)$ such that
$$\|V-I\|,\|W-I\|\le\sqrt\eta,\qquad \|D-VWV^*W^*\|\le40\eta^{3/2}.$$
lem-qc-two-axis-su2-generation:
## Statement

For a matrix $M$, write $e^M=\sum_{j\ge0}M^j/j!$. Write
$SU(2):=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=I_2,\det M=1\}$. Let
$a,b\in\mathbb R^3$ be nonparallel unit vectors, let $\sigma=(X,Y,Z)$ be the
Pauli triple, and put $A=i\,a\cdot\sigma$ and $B=i\,b\cdot\sigma$. If $H$ is
the operator-norm closure of the subgroup generated by
$\{e^{tA},e^{tB}:t\in\mathbb R\}$, then $H=SU(2)$.
lem-qc-clifford-t-projective-density:
## Statement

Use the Pauli matrices $X,Y,Z$ and exact gates $H=(X+Z)/\sqrt2$ and
$T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})$ from
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and
[[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. Write $PU(2)$ for the
quotient of $U(2)$ by its unit-modulus scalar matrices, equipped with the
quotient topology. Their normalized lifts $h=iH$ and
$t=e^{-i\pi/8}T$ lie in $SU(2)$ and generate a dense subgroup of $SU(2)$;
therefore the projective classes of $H,T$ generate a dense subgroup of
$PU(2)$.
lem-qc-commutator-error-cancellation:
## Statement

Let $V,W,\widetilde V,\widetilde W\in SU(2)$ and $0\le\eta\le1/16$, with
$\|V-I\|,\|W-I\|\le\sqrt\eta$ and
$\|\widetilde V-V\|,\|\widetilde W-W\|\le\eta$. Then
$$\|VWV^*W^*-\widetilde V\widetilde W\widetilde V^*\widetilde W^*\|\le4\eta^{3/2}.$$
alg-qc-solovay-kitaev-unitary-compiler:
## Definition

**Inputs:** A fixed inverse-closed dense gate package $G$ with the finite
base-net certificate $(\mathcal N_0,\eta_0,L_0)$ from
[[def-qc-inverse-closed-dense-su2-gate-set]], an exact-real target
$U\in SU(2)$, and a rational $0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$. This is an ideal
exact-real procedure: fixed-dimensional exact matrix arithmetic, matrix
logarithm/exponential, and exact comparisons are unit-cost operations. It is
not, by this definition alone, a finite Turing algorithm.

Set $\eta_{j+1}=64\eta_j^{3/2}$ for $j\ge0$. Choose the least integer
$J\ge0$ with $\eta_J\le\varepsilon$. Define $\operatorname{Compile}(U,j)$
recursively:

1. If $j=0$, return the first word $A\in\mathcal N_0$ with
   $\|U-A\|\le\eta_0$.
2. If $j>0$, set $A=\operatorname{Compile}(U,j-1)$ and $D=UA^*$.
   If $D=I$, set $V=W=I$. Otherwise apply the Pauli-coordinate construction
   in [[lem-qc-su2-balanced-commutator]] to $D$ and $\eta_{j-1}$, obtaining
   $V,W\in SU(2)$ with $D$ approximated by $VWV^*W^*$.
3. Set $B=\operatorname{Compile}(V,j-1)$ and
   $C=\operatorname{Compile}(W,j-1)$. Return the word
   $BCB^*C^*A$. Store concatenations and inverses as a shared expression DAG;
   an inverse word is formed by reversing its label order and replacing each
   label by its listed inverse. Expanding the DAG writes the ordinary gate word.

Return $\operatorname{Compile}(U,J)$. The recursion depth is finite because
each call decreases the nonnegative integer $j$.
thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-error-and-resource:
## Statement

For a fixed inverse-closed dense $G\subset SU(2)$ and a certified base net of
radius $0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$, the compiler of
[[alg-qc-solovay-kitaev-unitary-compiler]] returns, for
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, a word $W$ with
$\|U-W\|\le\varepsilon$. The level errors may be chosen as
$$\eta_j=64^{-2}(64^2\eta_0)^{(3/2)^j}.$$
The word length is $L_0 5^j$ at level $j$, hence
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
With shared recursive words, the exact-real arithmetic count is
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}3}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{2.71}(1/\varepsilon))$;
printing the expanded word takes $O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$ time.
The latter are exact-real arithmetic bounds, not bit-complexity bounds.
thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity:
## Statement

Fix a finite inverse-closed dense $G\subset SU(2)$ whose real and imaginary
gate-entry coordinates are algebraic numbers supplied by their minimal
polynomials over $\mathbb Q$ and rational isolating intervals with opposite
endpoint signs and exactly one real root, and fix a
rational certified base-net radius
$0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$. Let the finite base-net certificate be fixed. Suppose
$U\in SU(2)$ is given by a Cauchy name whose query on unary input $1^b$ takes
at most $(b+1)^c$ bit operations for a fixed integer $c\ge1$. Given rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$ in binary, there is a deterministic Turing
implementation of the Solovay–Kitaev recursion that outputs a gate word $W$
with $\|U-W\|\le\varepsilon$ and length
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))$. If $s_\varepsilon$ is the binary
encoding length of $\varepsilon$ and
$N=\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil$, its bit time, including reading
$\varepsilon$ and printing the expanded word, is
$$O\bigl((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10}\bigr).$$
The constants depend on $G$, the fixed base-net certificate, and the fixed
algebraic descriptions. This is distinct from the exact-real arithmetic
count in [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-error-and-resource-bound]].
thm-qc-fixed-arity-unitary-error-budget:
## Statement

Fix $k\ge1$, $U\in U(2^k)$, and a real $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Suppose a supplied exact decomposition of
$U$ has $m\ge1$ one-qubit $U(2)$ factors and $c\ge0$ exact CNOT factors,
with no ancillas. Compiling the special-unitary part of each one-qubit factor
to error $\varepsilon/m$ gives a circuit $C$ such that
$$\min_{|\lambda|=1}\|U-\lambda C\|\le\varepsilon.$$
Its gate count is at most
$c+O(m\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(m/\varepsilon))$ for fixed $k$ and fixed base net.
For every unit vector $\psi$ and every nonnegative contraction $E$ on the
$2^k$-dimensional space, the event value
$p_E(V,\psi):=\|E^{1/2}V\psi\|^2$ changes by at most $2\varepsilon$ between
$V=U$ and $V=C$. The phase guarantee is for the whole unconditional block.
Here nonnegative contraction means $E=E^*$, $\langle Ev,v\rangle\ge0$ for
all $v$, and $\|E\|\le1$.
thm-qc-controlled-phase-approximation:
## Statement

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let
$P_\alpha=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\alpha})$ and
$R_z(\alpha)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{-i\alpha/2},e^{i\alpha/2})$.
Define $CP_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{i\theta})$ in the
control-first basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$.
Define CNOT by $|a,b\rangle\mapsto|a,b\oplus a\rangle$, where
$a,b\in\{0,1\}$ and $\oplus$ is addition modulo two. The continuous
phase-gate model permits each $P_\alpha$ exactly for real $\alpha$.
On an additional control qubit define
$C(M)=\operatorname{diag}(I_4,M)$ in control-first order. The two-qubit
circuit that applies CNOT, then $P_{-\theta/2}$ to the target, then CNOT,
then $P_{\theta/2}$ to each wire implements $CP_\theta$. Replacing the
three $P$ gates by their $R_z$ representatives gives
$e^{-i\theta/4}CP_\theta$; here
$P_\alpha=e^{i\alpha/2}R_z(\alpha)$.

For the three-qubit factorization, use the lexicographically ordered basis
$|a,b,c\rangle$ with $a,b,c\in\{0,1\}$. A gate $P_\alpha^{(j)}$ multiplies
this basis vector by $e^{i\alpha x_j}$, where $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(a,b,c)$;
$\operatorname{CNOT}_{i\to j}$ toggles bit $x_j$ by $x_i$ and fixes the
other bits. These explicit basis actions fix the wire order used below.

The fixed-arity compiler gives a projective operator approximation within
$\varepsilon$ when applied to the complete $CP_\theta$ block. If this block
is controlled by an additional qubit, the compiler must instead be applied
to the complete three-qubit controlled-$CP_\theta$ matrix. A phase-minimized
approximation to $CP_\theta$ cannot in general be controlled without
restoring its relative phase. In particular, controlling the $R_z$ circuit
from the first paragraph gives
$C(e^{-i\theta/4}CP_\theta)=
(\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{-i\theta/4})\otimes I_4)C(CP_\theta)$;
applying $P_{\theta/4}$ to the added control restores the exact controlled
target in the continuous phase-gate model.
ex-qc-solovay-kitaev-error-budget:
## Statement

Suppose a fixed three-factor unitary block is $U=G_3G_2G_1$, where each
$G_j=e^{i\phi_j}S_j$ with $S_j\in SU(2)$. If words $W_j$ satisfy
$\|S_j-W_j\|\le\varepsilon/3$, then the word product
$C=W_3W_2W_1$ satisfies
$\min_{|\lambda|=1}\|U-\lambda C\|\le\varepsilon$.
